links.outcome: Whether pathologist review corrects AI errors in ACIS and suspected SCC calls
links.effect: After adjudication (EE + P2), ACIS restored from 13/20 to 18/20 and SCC calls reduced from 4 to 1 of 20; 6 of 7 AI-flagged SCC in P1-CIN3 retained.
links.quote: After expert adjudication in the EE + P2 condition, ACIS was restored to 18/20 and SCC was reduced to 1/20, demonstrating that the human reviewer corrected virtually all high-consequence AI errors.

links.outcome: CIN2+ calling with vs without AI assistance for the same pathologist
links.effect: EE + P2 identified 69 CIN2+ vs P2 alone 70; agreement with P2-digital 90.7% (κ 0.79) for EE+P2 vs 88.7% (κ 0.74) for EE alone; P1 sensitivity 83.8% vs AI-assisted reference; no significant shift (p=1.00).
links.quote: These findings indicate that, for the high-volume expert reader, the AI-assisted workflow (EE + P2) did not significantly alter the overall CIN2+ calling rate relative to unaided digital review, but rather redistributed a small number of borderline cases in both directions.

links.outcome: AI performance compared against original pathologist sign-out at CIN2+ threshold
links.effect: Using P1 as reference, EagleEye sensitivity 93.3% (56/60), specificity 71.8% (28/39); agreement with P1 κ=0.67.
links.quote: Against P1 as reference, EE identified 56/60 CIN2+ cases (sensitivity 93.3%) with specificity 71.8% (28/39), corresponding to 11 false positives (P1 <CIN2) and 4 false negatives.

links.outcome: Representativeness and generalizability of test data (single-centre, spectrum-balanced, prevalence-inflated)
links.effect: Single centre, one scanner, spectrum-balanced convenience sample with inflated CIN2+ prevalence (~60–70%); PPV/NPV would be lower at 5–10% prevalence; external validation needed.
links.quote: Second, the dataset was intentionally spectrum-balanced with a much higher CIN2+/ACIS prevalence than in routine screening or ordinary referral cohorts; this spectrum bias inflates PPV/NPV and may also influence κ, so predictive values reported here should be considered study-internal and would be lower at 5–10% CIN2+ prevalence.

links.outcome: Adequacy of reference standard for accuracy estimates
links.effect: No independent gold standard; P1 sign-out and AI-assisted EE+P2 used as references, the latter subject to incorporation/verification bias.
links.quote: Because EE + P2 incorporates the intervention under study, this comparison is subject to verification/incorporation bias and is presented strictly as an internal case-finding exploration rather than as a formal estimate of P1 diagnostic accuracy; all sensitivity/specificity estimates versus EE + P2 should therefore be interpreted as study-internal performance metrics, not as externally generalizable truth standards.

links.outcome: Justification of decision threshold for AI slide-level positivity
links.effect: The ≥15-tile operating point was chosen heuristically, not from ROC or decision-curve analysis; no continuous score or tunable operating point.
links.quote: The threshold was not derived from formal ROC or decision-curve calibration and is therefore reported as a methodological limitation.

links.outcome: Multi-site and device validation of AI performance
links.effect: Validation was on a single site with one scanner and one H&E protocol; multi-site validation across scanners and staining protocols identified as required.
links.quote: First, this was an internal, single-center study from a single Norwegian university hospital, with its own screening routines, case mix, HPV vaccination coverage and referral patterns, using one H&E protocol and one scanner.

links.outcome: AI false negatives and overcalls that clinician review must catch
links.effect: EE had 4 false negatives and 11 false positives vs P1; under-called ACIS (13/20) with 3 downgraded to CIN1; pathologist review corrected most errors.
links.quote: EE alone under-called ACIS (13/20) and redistributed the remainder in both clinically unfavorable directions—downward to CIN1 (n = 3), which represents a potential false negative at the treatment threshold, and upward to SCC (n = 4), which represents a false positive invasive call ( Table 9 ).

links.outcome: AI accuracy for rare glandular lesions (ACIS) versus squamous disease
links.effect: EagleEye alone called ACIS in 13/20 cases; performance clearly weaker than for squamous disease, attributed to sparse training data.
links.quote: Performance on glandular lesions was clearly weaker than on squamous disease.

links.outcome: AI-assisted versus unaided expert digital reading
links.effect: P2-digital vs EE+P2: sensitivity 92.8%, specificity 86.7%; 4 apparent false positives, 5 apparent false negatives; McNemar p=1.00.
links.quote: These findings indicate that, for the high-volume expert reader, the AI-assisted workflow (EE + P2) did not significantly alter the overall CIN2+ calling rate relative to unaided digital review, but rather redistributed a small number of borderline cases in both directions.

links.outcome: AI-alone missed or downgraded lesions
links.effect: EE alone under-called ACIS 13/20; downgraded to CIN1 n = 3 and upgraded to SCC n = 4.
links.quote: Pathologists showed high concordance on glandular disease (P2: 19–20/20 ACIS, with only a single digital downgrade), whereas EE alone under-called ACIS (13/20) and redistributed the remainder in both clinically unfavorable directions—downward to CIN1 (n = 3), which represents a potential false negative at the treatment threshold, and upward to SCC (n = 4), which represents a false positive invasive call ( Table 9 ).

links.outcome: Adjunct AI with pathologist final authority
links.effect: EagleEye reached 93.3% sensitivity and 71.8% specificity; AI guidance surfaced additional CIN2+ while final responsibility remained with pathologists.
links.quote: Taken together, these findings support EagleEye as a safety-net decision-support tool that can reduce the risk of missed high-grade lesions and promote more consistent grading of cervical biopsies, while final diagnostic responsibility remains with the pathologist.

links.outcome: Expert detection of incorrect AI outputs
links.effect: After adjudication, ACIS increased from EE-alone 13/20 to 18/20, and false invasive SCC calls decreased to 1/20.
links.quote: After expert adjudication in the EE + P2 condition, ACIS was restored to 18/20 and false invasive calls were largely removed (SCC 1/20).

links.outcome: AI-alone diagnostic accuracy errors
links.effect: Against P1, EE sensitivity was 93.3% and specificity 71.8%, with 11 false positives and 4 false negatives.
links.quote: Against P1 as reference, EE identified 56/60 CIN2+ cases (sensitivity 93.3%) with specificity 71.8% (28/39), corresponding to 11 false positives (P1 <CIN2) and 4 false negatives.
